Dynarmic is vendored with its bundled dependencies. nixe-cpu-jit builds it
for A64 guests. The license is 0BSD (LICENSE.txt), with GPL-3.0-or-later
additions identified in source headers, including the register allocator
additions and the A64 PAuth and LSE translators. Bundled dependencies retain
their own licenses.

Nixe adaptations

- On x64, A64 memory callbacks can terminate execution on a host failure
  without retaining precise recoverable guest state at every ordinary access.
  The native bridge selects the memory policy independently of ARM ISA
  extensions. Callback guards exit immediately on cancellation or failure.
  The configuration interface also supports precise recoverable memory aborts.
- backend/x64/a64_emit_x64 omits halt checks on forward links within a code
  page when cycle counting is disabled. The emitter checks the page boundary
  at compile time. Backward links, indirect exits and page crossings keep
  their halt checks. Cycle-counted and single-step execution retain theirs.
- backend/x64/{a64_emit_x64,emit_x64,emit_x64_data_processing,block_of_code}
  reuses host flags from adjacent arithmetic operations for NZCV and from
  the final check-bit operation in no-cycle mode. The emitter preserves
  committed guest flags and carry polarity. It checks emission positions
  within a single block and treats immediates and callbacks conservatively.
  Verbose instrumentation and cycle-counted terminals store check bits explicitly.
- backend/{code_cache_hash,block_range_information}, backend/x64/{emit_x64,
  a64_emit_x64} and the ARM64-host descriptor owners use the mcl XMRX mixer
  on the full PC/context key for robin maps and sets. This covers incoming
  block references, invalidation and fastmem markers. Containers that already
  mix their hashes use the standard hashes.
- backend/x64/a64_emit_x64 uses a cache-line-aligned, four-way fast dispatch
  table with 2^16 entries, full tags and FIFO insertion. It publishes the tag
  after the C++ lookup, which can clear the cache on capacity exhaustion.
  Invalidation retires exact tag matches across all four ways. A64's 32-entry
  software return stack supplies the bounds for entry lookup, push/pop masks,
  state offsets and invalidation resets.
- backend/x64/{a64_emit_x64,emit_x64_data_processing,emit_x64_memory} folds
  single-use scalar base-plus-displacement additions into unchecked fastmem
  operands. IR instructions carry their own emission markers. The emitter
  preserves full callback addresses, inverse/base restoration, store aliases,
  precise memory aborts and deoptimization. Recovery and fault trampolines use
  the cold code region.
- Diagnostic builds count generated dispatch hits and misses, return-stack
  hits, and the bytes emitted in the near and cold regions separately.
- backend/x64/{block_of_code,a64_emit_x64,emit_x64_memory} shares compact
  A64 exit stubs. The cold region uses the final quarter of the existing
  allocation, or seven-sixteenths when precise memory-abort recovery needs
  larger stubs. Each region has its own write bound, Windows memory
  commitment and protection, and symbol and disassembly coverage. Deferred
  captures remain reusable inline. Stubs preserve per-transition halt checks,
  precise fault metadata and epoch ownership.
- The native bridge assumes valid guest addresses in commercial games and
  omits fastmem-width checks. Arena and page-table bounds, page permissions
  and coherent fault handling still apply. The configuration boundary documents
  the simplification. Other native configurations can use bounded fastmem.
- backend/x64/{emit_x64,emit_x64_data_processing,a64_emit_x64} omits redundant
  U32-to-U64 normalization for producers known to clear the upper bits.
  Widening aliases require a general-purpose register. Partial-width spill
  slots are normalized before 64-bit use. A64 selects the policy through its
  code buffer. A32 uses its normal emission path.
- backend/x64/reg_alloc preserves evicted values in free callee-saved registers
  where the ABI allows it. It copies writable live operands into free registers
  before spilling. The allocator computes the ABI and admission spill-candidate
  mask once, records allocation locations on the IR and tracks releases per
  scope. The native bridge enables these options for A64.
- backend/block_range_information stores compiled guest extents in a contiguous
  vector. Invalidation uses the interval set's logarithmic overlap lookup to
  retire intersecting entries. Extents retain their compilation context and
  inclusive u32/u64 endpoints. Cache clears reuse the vector's capacity. Both
  x64 and ARM64 hosts clear extent records on explicit and capacity-triggered
  resets. On ARM64 the virtual cache-clear boundary covers both A32 and A64.
- backend/x64/{perf_map,emit_x64,a32_emit_x64_memory,a64_emit_x64_memory,
  block_of_code} checks PERF_BUILDID_DIR once. When disabled, it skips symbol
  name formatting and the process-wide map mutex. Linux tracks live symbols
  by code range and rebuilds the perf map when a range retires, preserving
  other JITs and the owner's prelude. New allocations retire old names at
  reused addresses. Teardown retains the last map for postmortem sampling.
  Non-Linux symbol operations compile to inline no-ops.
- DYNARMIC_JIT_DIAGNOSTICS, enabled by the Rust performance-counters feature,
  records per-JIT lookup and compilation counters, instruction fingerprints,
  phase timings, and mainline and deferred code sizes. It distinguishes
  capacity resets, requested clears, targeted invalidations and fastmem
  invalidations. The native bridge buffers events for offline epoch analysis.
  Production builds omit the diagnostic fields, counters, clocks and callbacks.
  Fingerprints are diagnostic only.
- backend/exception_handler{.h,_posix.cpp} exposes cold fault resolution.
  DYNARMIC_EXTERNAL_FAULT_HANDLER lets Nixe own POSIX signal capture.
- backend/x64/a64_emit_x64.cpp checks halt and budget conditions at linked,
  indirect and return transitions to bound scheduler preemption and memory
  transitions.
- backend/x64/a64_emit_x64.cpp emits wall-clock CNTPCT reads inline when the
  client supplies a stable host TSC, a shared atomic clock base and a fixed-point
  frequency multiplier. The sample retries across pause/resume publication.
  Other clocks and host backends retain the counter callback.
- backend/x64/emit_x64_memory uses the canonical page table for exclusive
  loads and compare/exchange after fastmem deoptimization. A64 accepts a
  separate read mark so ordinary read-only pages remain directly readable.
  Marked, absent and unsupported unaligned accesses retain their callbacks.
  Sign-extended pointer masks use an immediate and one address register.
- backend/x64 stores A64 fastmem fault sites in the owning JIT. The emitter
  looks up the block once and borrows its marked IR instructions for both
  address folding and emission, without shared locking or copying.
- The x64 A64 JIT resolves captured faults against its own memory sites. Nixe
  can restore an evicted host alias and finish the faulting access through the
  generated callback without marking the site or recompiling its block.
- frontend/A64/translate/impl/sys_dc.cpp ends blocks after cache operations.
  Nixe applies ownership transitions after releasing its execution lease.
- ir/opt/a64_get_set_elimination_pass.cpp, ir/opt/passes.h and both A64
  backends retain register setters visible at memory-abort exits while
  forwarding register values and eliminating redundant accesses.
- interface/A64/config.h, frontend/A64/translate and both A64 backends can
  stop at unknown extension HINTs on newer guest CPUs.
- A64 pointer authentication uses an unsigned-pointer model selected at
  translation time. PAC, AUT and XPAC emit no host instructions. PACGA uses
  masked XOR. Authenticated branches and loads use plain addresses. This
  removes per-process keys, the QARMA helper, the PAuth IR opcode, its host
  emitters and PAuth-specific address checks at entry, dispatch and return.
  Code fetches and memory accesses retain their ordinary permission checks.
  The translator marks the approximation @SIMPLIFICATION and @SPECULATIVE.
- frontend/A64/translate/impl/load_store_atomic.cpp selects LSE operations at
  translation time. Exclusive IR implements CAS/CASP, SWP and atomic ALU
  operations with acquire/release ordering and retries without partial register
  updates. With RCpc enabled, LDAPR uses limited-order acquire operations.
  A64CheckMemoryAlignment in both host backends faults before a misaligned
  atomic operation. Precise memory exits preserve earlier register setters.

The native bridge allocates a 512 MiB code cache per JIT on x64 except on
Solaris, NetBSD, DragonFly and OpenBSD. Those systems and other hosts use
128 MiB. Each JIT owns its executable allocation. The backend manages demand
residency and both full and targeted invalidation.

The Rust/C ABI integration lives in crates/cpu-jit. The interpreter and the JIT
share native fault capture through cpu-direct-memory.
